News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Sat, 28 Nov 2026 02:03:13 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title><![CDATA[S&P revises France's outlook from 'stable' to 'negative']]></title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261127-s-p-revises-france-s-outlook-from-stable-to-negative</link><description><![CDATA[
Rating agency S&P revised France’s outlook to "negative" from "stable" on Friday, citing growing budget pressures as weak economic growth and higher interest costs make it harder to reduce the deficit.
]]></description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c550db02-eaab-11f1-9bac-174dac1c1bf0/w:1024/p:16x9/AP16236824377278.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c550db02-eaab-11f1-9bac-174dac1c1bf0/w:1024/p:16x9/AP16236824377278.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7fd5dec4-eaab-11f1-8d75-95f9105a3c8e</guid><pubDate>Fri, 27 Nov 2026 22:00:20 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c550db02-eaab-11f1-9bac-174dac1c1bf0/w:1024/p:16x9/AP16236824377278.jpg">© Henny Ray Abrams, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Eye on Africa</category><title>Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/eye-on-africa/20261127-uganda-to-withdraw-troops-from-dr-congo</link><description>
First, Uganda is heading for the exit in eastern DR Congo. Kampala has announced the withdrawal of its troops from a key town in North Kivu, as relations with Kinshasa deteriorate following provocative comments from Uganda's army chief. Then, pregnant women are struggling to cope with extreme heat, while health experts warn of growing risks for unborn babies, from dehydration to premature births. And, after seeking safety, opportunity and a better life, many migrants in South Africa now face hostility, violence and growing exclusion. As anti-immigration sentiment gains ground, the country's promise is fading for those who once saw it as a land of hope.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/92a9d6c2-eaa6-11f1-8c67-1991d4929b54/w:1024/p:16x9/DL00006224-VOD-00023676-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/92a9d6c2-eaa6-11f1-8c67-1991d4929b54/w:1024/p:16x9/DL00006224-VOD-00023676-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2f58a35a-eaab-11f1-873d-95f9105a3c8e</guid><pubDate>Fri, 27 Nov 2026 21:44:29 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Clarisse FORTUNÉ</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Ukraine submits Black Sea ceasefire offer, awaits Russian response</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261127-ukraine-submits-black-sea-ceasefire-offer-awaits-russian-response</link><description>
⁠Ukraine ​made a Black Sea ceasefire offer ​to enable food exports and passed the details on to international allies, a senior Ukrainian official said Friday, adding that Kyiv was waiting for a response from Moscow. The announcement came a day after Russia attacked ​two foreign grain carriers near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, according to Ukrainian authorities.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/62fe879a-ea9e-11f1-912c-174dac1c1bf0/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26200564414743.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/62fe879a-ea9e-11f1-912c-174dac1c1bf0/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26200564414743.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">833df95a-ea9e-11f1-9aa1-839a2a2043d0</guid><pubDate>Fri, 27 Nov 2026 21:09:12 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/62fe879a-ea9e-11f1-912c-174dac1c1bf0/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26200564414743.jpg">© Michael Shtekel, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>Spanish elections: 'Right-wing voters extremely mobilised, left-wing voters not mobilised enough'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261127-spanish-elections-right-wing-voters-extremely-mobilised-left-wing-voters-not-mobilised-enough</link><description>
“His main political platform is to say, I am not Sánchez, I am the opposite of Sánchez.” As Spain heads to the polls, what do Alberto Núñez Feijóo's campaign and political career tell us about the kind of prime minister he might become? Javier Carbonell, Policy Analyst at the European Politics and Institutions Programme and lecturer at Sciences Po in Paris, joins Gavin Lee to break down the Popular Party leader's efforts to avoid the mistakes of 2023 and keep right-wing voters mobilised without galvanising the left.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/18289436-ea9e-11f1-891f-81bc2b1dcd65/w:1024/p:16x9/NW304504-O-01-20261127-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/18289436-ea9e-11f1-891f-81bc2b1dcd65/w:1024/p:16x9/NW304504-O-01-20261127-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3d78daf2-eaa3-11f1-8f58-e3c283b84dce</guid><pubDate>Fri, 27 Nov 2026 20:43:44 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>The World This Week</category><title><![CDATA[The End of Spain’s ‘Frankenstein’ Coalition? Presidential Plotting in Paris, Kushner & Kremlin Trap]]></title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/the-world-this-week/20261127-the-end-of-spain-s-frankenstein-coalition-presidential-plotting-in-paris-kushner-kremlin-trap</link><description>
Catch up with the World This Week with Gavin Lee. In just 45 minutes, make sense of seven extraordinary days in global affairs, as Gavin and his handpicked panel of four leading international correspondents unpack the stories shaping the world — and the questions behind the headlines.
 
This week: Spain’s snap election; the presidential plotting unfolding over lunch at the Brasserie Concorde in Paris; Ukraine, Kushner and the ‘Kremlin Trap’; and the question hanging over Iran: whose side is time on?
 
Joining Gavin are New World Magazine columnist Emma-Kate Symonds; Constant Méheut, The New York Times correspondent in Ukraine; Venetia Rainer, Daily Telegraph Foreign Editor and host of Iran: The Latest; and Sarah Morris, France 24’s correspondent in Spain.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4df96bdc-ea9c-11f1-a0ee-1991d4929b54/w:1024/p:16x9/6c11ec77-814a-4283-a56b-ff1aabd888a2.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4df96bdc-ea9c-11f1-a0ee-1991d4929b54/w:1024/p:16x9/6c11ec77-814a-4283-a56b-ff1aabd888a2.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2bef1dea-ea9f-11f1-92a3-239ede51fb3e</guid><pubDate>Fri, 27 Nov 2026 20:14:37 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

]]> <![CDATA[ Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still ]]> Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W.

It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination.

But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper/the Plough. It's gone.

Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn.

What's happening and when to look

Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3.

This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations, it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris, the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon.

This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract.

How and when I'm watching it

I'm going to observe Cassiopeia twice on the same evening this week, which is about as complicated as the experiment needs to get. The first time will be shortly after darkness falls. I'll find the W, note which way it seems to be pointing and use something fixed — a rooftop, tree or chimney — to give myself a rough reference for its position. I'll return to my backyard before bed, and see where the pattern has shifted. Cassiopeia's main stars are bright enough to survive urban and suburban light pollution, so you don't need a particularly dark sky or a telescope.

While I'm gazing at Cassiopeia, I'll try to see the stars as they really are, and not just how they appear to us. Check out the distances of its stars from the sun:

  • Caph: 55 light-years

On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor.

The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic.

The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower. The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet, which broke apart in the 1850s.

When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm. This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour.

Why it mattered

Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible.

But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name).

Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors.

In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023.

      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/ekonomika/domaci/s-darky-letos-poradi-ai-cesi-ji-sveri-vyber-pro-babicku-i-manzela.A261118_144740_ekonomika_vebe#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Při výběru dárků letos poprvé sehraje výraznou roli umělá inteligence. Češi se už naučili využívat AI k řadě úkolů a nezdráhají se chatbotům popsat zájmy svých blízkých, rozpočet i termín doručení a nechat si navrhnout konkrétní výrobky. Muž bez domova teď daroval muzeu svůj poklad</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906863-vsechno-zacalo-jednou-prohlidkou-muz-bez-domova-ted-daroval-muzeu-svuj-poklad.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906863-vsechno-zacalo-jednou-prohlidkou-muz-bez-domova-ted-daroval-muzeu-svuj-poklad.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Stačila jediná návštěva Automoto Musea v Lučanech, aby se zrodil silný lidský příběh.  <description><div id="cke_pastebin" style="position: absolute; left: -1000px; top: 12px; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden;">

<div>
<div>
		Tradiční podzimní bod programu je zpět – němý film za doprovodu živé hudby.&nbsp;Daniel Karko patří k nejvýraznějším hudebníkům nastupující českolipské generace. Za poslední tři roky jsem ho potkal hned ve čtyřech uskupeních – Rise of Nowhere, Tajnej Lionel, Obejmi tátu a duo Rýže. V listopadu se představí v netradiční roli: s vlastním hudebním doprovodem oživí v kině dobrodružný němý film Ztracený svět z roku 1925. Jeho první rozhovor tak nemohl přijít v lepší chvíli.</div>

výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu dobrý den ze šluknovského výběžku, konce světa - šluknovský výběžek Fri, 27 Nov 2026 19:03:06 +0000 cs hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.5 https://www.vybezek.eu/wp-uploads/2018/09/cropped-favicon-vybezek-32x32.png výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu 32 32 Podzimní hry 2026 – bruslení – 5. kolo podzimních her aneb souboj na ledě https://www.vybezek.eu/297956-podzimni-hry-2026-brusleni-5-kolo-podzimnich-her-aneb-souboj-na-lede/ Fri, 27 Nov 2026 19:03:06 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=297956 V pátek 27. listopadu 2026 se na zimním stadionu ve Varnsdorfu uskutečnilo již 5. kolo podzimních her, tentokrát v bruslení.

Soutěže se zúčastnila čtyři družstva ze čtyř varnsdorfských škol. Každou školu reprezentovalo osm žáků – čtyři chlapci a čtyři dívky. Soutěž probíhala formou štafetového závodu, ve kterém o konečném umístění rozhodoval výsledný čas celé štafety. Důležitá tak byla nejen rychlost a obratnost na ledě, ale také týmová spolupráce.

Souboj o první místo byl velmi těsný. Gymnázium Varnsdorf zvítězilo před ZŠ Východní s náskokem pouhých dvou sekund. Družstvo naší školy vybojovalo krásné třetí místo.

Výsledkové pořadí:

1. místo – Gymnázium Varnsdorf (4:34)
2. místo – ZŠ Východní (4:36)
3. místo – ZŠ Náměstí (5:09)
4. místo – ZŠ Edisonova (6:00)

Naši žáci rozhodně neudělali na ledě ostudu. Poctivě bojovali, nevzdávali se a s odhodláním reprezentovali naši školu. Všem osmi závodníkům patří velké poděkování za jejich nasazení, bojovnost a sportovního ducha.

Nyní už nezbývá než se těšit na šesté a zároveň poslední kolo letošních podzimních her, které se ponese ve znamení florbalu.

Děkujeme za reprezentaci školy a držíme palce do závěrečného kola!

Mgr. Lukáš Hůla, ZŠ Varnsdorf, nám. E. Beneše
